aggressive_definition: Incident advanced (extraprostatic), fatal, or high-grade (Gleason score ≥7) prostate cancer.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Over 16 years of follow-up, we identified 3,544 total cases of prostate cancer, 523 advanced (extraprostatic) cases, and 312 fatal cases.
study_design: Prospective cohort study using the Health Professionals Follow-up Study.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We examined calcium intake in relation to prostate cancer risk using data from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study, a prospective cohort study of 47,750 male health professionals with no history of cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer at baseline.
reason: The initially cancer-free prospective cohort was analyzed for total incident prostate cancer and multiple aggressive incident endpoints, including advanced, fatal, and high-grade disease. The aggressive case count records the reported advanced-case count; the abstract also reports 312 fatal cases but no high-grade case count.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For high-grade prostate cancer (Gleason > or = 7), an association was observed for high versus low calcium intake (RR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.32-2.71; P(trend) = 0.005), but a nonsignificant, inverse association was observed for organ-confined, low-grade prostate cancer (RR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.50-1.25; P(trend) = 0.09).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns incident high-grade prostate cancer defined as Gleason score ≥7.
